previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her seventh cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well, with expected mild transaminitis and stable mild anemia. Her methotrexate levels cleared appropriately, allowing for IV leucovorin rescue without the need for oral leucovorin or bicarbonate at discharge. Chronic right foot pain, likely neuropathic, persisted but was managed with increased gabapentin and PRN analgesics. She remained neurologically stable, with recent imaging showing continued improvement in her brain lesion. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans to continue enoxaparin, adjust medications, and return in two weeks for her next chemotherapy cycle.

Brief Hospital Course:
A/P: ___ woman with UC, asthma, DVT/PE, and CNS lymphoma 
admitted for cycle #8 high-dose methotrexate. Previous MRI 
showed CR.  
.  
# CNS lymphoma: Received ___ cycle #8 high-dose MTX 8g/m2. 
Creatinine clearance 135mL/hr. She will require one more cycles 
at q2wks before switching to monthly doses per Neuro-onc. She 
should have a repeat MRI at cycle #9 on her next admission. 
Chemo included: 
- Bicarb: 1meq/kg IV prior to MTX, 25meq IV with chemo, 50meq/L 
bicarb in IV fluids, 1300mg PO q2HR PRN to maintain urine pH 
>7.5-8.5 to enhance MTX excretion.  
- MTX levels were followed daily 24hr post-chemo.  
- Leucovorin rescue PO/IV q6hrs started 24hrs after MTX.  
- Anti-emetics PRN.  
- Continued levetiracetam 500mg BID.  
- Continued acyclovir prophylaxis given hx of oral herpes.  
- MTX on morning of the day of discharge: 0.13. she continued 
alkalanized  IVF and leucovorin until discharge in mid afternoon 
so her level should have dropped < 0.10 by the time of DC. She 
was therefore not DC'd with bicarb and leucovorin.  
. 
# Nausea and vomiting: due to chemotherapy. now resolved. 
continued scheduled zofran. Received prn ativan IV, zofran IV, 
compazine po. Also tried promethazine IV prn.
.
# Hypokalemia: resolved. repleted with IV sliding scale. due to 
IVF.
.
# Hypophosphatemia: resolved. repleted with po neutraphos.
.
# Anemia: Due to maligancy/inflammation and chemo. Mild. Stable. 
 
.  
# Right foot pain: No clear cause. Perhaps neuropathic. Prior 
work up has included: MRI spine and lumbar puncture negative. 
Doppler U/S negative. X-ray normal. Transiently improved this 
admission now back to baseline. continued gabapentin from 600mg 
TID. Oxycodone and acetaminophen PRN. Will Consider MRI foot and 
repeat MRI L-spine.  
.  
# Transaminitis: Due to chemo, occurs with each cycle. Consider 
increasing leucovorin dose.  
.  
# LLE DVT/PE: Continued outpatient enoxaparin.  
.  
# Ulcerative colitis: Held mesalamine given its interaction with 
methotrexate. Will restart at discharge.  
.  
# Asthma: Continued outpatient fluticasone/salmeterol, 
montelukast, and albuterol PRN.  
.  
# Nausea: Anti-emetics premed and PRN.  
.  
# Headache: Resolved the morning of discharge. Unclear etiology. 
? Zofran with chemotherapy. Acetaminophen and oxycodone

citric acid to promote alkalosis. IV fluids per protocol. 
Metabolic alkalosis expected due to bicarb administration. 
Repleted hypokalemia.

# DVT prophylaxis: Enoxaparin for DVT.  
.  
# GI prophylaxis: D/C'd ranitidine since steroids finished (no

HISTORY:  CNS lymphoma for high-dose MTX, rule out pleural effusion.

CHEST, SINGLE AP PORTABLE VIEW.

There is right convex scoliosis.  Allowing for this, the cardiomediastinal
silhouette is likely within normal limits.  A right-sided Port-A-Cath type
catheter is present, with tip at SVC/RA junction.  No CHF, focal infiltrate,
effusion, or pneumothorax is detected.  Within the limits of plain film
radiography, no pulmonary nodules are identified.  Mild-to-moderate
degenerative changes in the mid thoracic spine, along the concavity of the
thoracic curve, are noted.

line has been removed and a Port-A-Cath has been placed.  Otherwise, I doubt
significant interval change.
